_about: Public-domain Thomas Erskine of Linlathen (1788-1870, Scottish lay theologian) for the Word Hoard: Remarks on the Internal Evidence for the Truth of Revealed Religion (1821), An Essay on Faith (1822), The Unconditional Freeness of the Gospel (1828), The Brazen Serpent (1831), The Doctrine of Election (1837), The Spiritual Order (1871) and his Letters, ed. William Hanna (2 vols, 1877), from Internet Archive scans. Not Ralph or Ebenezer Erskine, who have their own shelf. Added 2026-10-18 by lane A, round 31 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

terskine-internal-evidence: Remarks on the Internal Evidence for the Truth of Revealed Religion (Edinburgh: Waugh & Innes, 1821)
terskine-essay-on-faith: An Essay on Faith, second edition (Edinburgh: Waugh and Innes, 1822)
terskine-unconditional-freeness: The Unconditional Freeness of the Gospel, from the second Edinburgh edition (Boston: Crocker and Brewster, 1828)
terskine-brazen-serpent: The Brazen Serpent; or, Life Coming through Death, second edition (Edinburgh: Waugh & Innes, M.DCCC.XXXI)
terskine-doctrine-of-election: The Doctrine of Election (London: James Duncan, M DCCC XXXVII)
terskine-spiritual-order: The Spiritual Order and Other Papers (Edinburgh: Edmonston and Douglas, 1871)
terskine-letters-1: Letters of Thomas Erskine of Linlathen, 1800-1840, ed. William Hanna (Edinburgh: David Douglas, 1877)
terskine-letters-2: Letters of Thomas Erskine of Linlathen, 1840-1870, ed. William Hanna (Edinburgh: David Douglas, 1877)

_alternates.terskine-copies: Later editions of Remarks (1821-1878), the 1829 Edinburgh Unconditional Freeness and 1870-1879 issues, the 1879 Brazen Serpent, the 1878 Election, the 1876 Spiritual Order, the 1878 and 1884 Letters
